title: Design review feedback loop
idea: Peer review is asking another engineer to read your design and code, find weak spots, and then deciding which comments change the design.
points: Share the class diagram, the requirements and your assumptions before the code.
Ask reviewers specific questions, such as "is `ConflictPolicy` the right seam?"
Sort each comment: fix now, discuss, or note as a known trade-off.
Reply to every comment, so reviewers see what changed and why.

items.label: Self-review
items.text: Check names, one job per class and passing tests before anyone reads it.

items.label: Share
items.text: Send the diagram, use cases and two or three questions you want answered.

items.label: Review
items.text: A peer reads it, for example asking who should send the cancellation notice.

items.label: Triage
items.text: Mark each comment as fix now, discuss, or accepted trade-off.

items.label: Respond
items.text: Change the design, rerun the tests, and reply with what you did.

quiz.q: A reviewer says `BookingService` should also send emails directly. What is the best response?
options: Agree at once, since reviewers are usually right
Ignore it, because the design is already finished
Explain why `NotificationService` owns emails, then ask their concern
Delete `NotificationService` to keep the class count low
quiz.why: Good review is a discussion. You defend the separation with a reason and look for the real concern behind the comment.

takeaway: Ask focused questions, triage every comment, and show what changed.

starters: What should I ask a reviewer to look at in my booking design?
How do I handle a review comment I disagree with?
What makes a review comment useful rather than vague?
